source: NaCCA Creative Arts Curriculum for Primary Schools (Basic 1–3), September 2019; themes grounded in the supplied curriculum passages
accessibility: Prompts may be read aloud. Accept oral, written, drawing, movement or demonstration responses as appropriate. Use teacher-provided examples where needed; do not require private disclosure, travel, purchases or public performance.
note: Questions are grouped under curriculum-aligned indicator themes. The supplied document retrieval exposed the Basic 3 section and scope but not its complete indicator tables; codes below are provisional and must not be treated as verbatim verified codes.

indicators.statement: Explore local visual artworks and how they reflect community history, culture and way of life.
questions: Which can help learners understand a local artwork?
A reliable explanation of its use or history
Name one visual artwork found in a community.
Basket, pot, carving, textile, poster or drawing
Describe one feature of a pictured artwork.
Colour, shape, line, pattern, texture or material
Which may be a useful artwork?
A basket used to carry items
Name one material used in local artworks.
Clay, wood, fibre, paper or fabric
You are unsure what a symbol means. What should you do?
Ask a teacher or knowledgeable source; do not guess as fact
Match: pot; basket; poster to likely use.
holds items; carries items; shares a message
Draw or describe an artwork inspired by a verified local example.
Why can artworks help show culture?
They may use meaningful forms, materials or patterns
Name one way to learn about an artwork respectfully.
Observe, read a label or ask politely
What question could you ask an artist about their work?
A respectful question about process or meaning
A classmate has a different interpretation. What is a good response?
What should a learner do with uncertain cultural details?
Name one feature that makes an artwork recognisable.
Distinctive shape, pattern, material or purpose
Match: line; texture; pattern to feature descriptions.
Practise a polite question about a teacher-provided artwork.
Which is a respectful way to compare artworks?
Describe their features without ranking cultures
How can people preserve knowledge about local artworks?
Identify one artwork and explain its material and possible use.
Plausible material and use based on evidence
Why should we avoid mocking unfamiliar artworks?
They may be important to a community's heritage

indicators.statement: Observe natural and man-made environments and develop visual ideas from them.
questions: Road, school, bridge, house or tool
Name two features you can observe in a leaf.
Shape, colour, veins, size or texture
Match: cloud; building; tree to natural or man-made.
Explain one way a natural object can inspire a design.
Its shape, pattern, colour or texture can be used
Draw a place with one natural and one built feature.
You want to use a living flower as a sample. What is a better choice?
Observe, draw or use a provided image without picking it
Which is a safe way to gather ideas outside?
Observe without damaging plants or disturbing animals
What can repeated leaf shapes make?
Name one material that can be reused safely for a model.
Clean paper or cardboard, with teacher approval
A found object is dirty or sharp. What should you do?
Do not handle it; tell the teacher
Match: pencil; crayon; clay with sketch; colouring; modelling.
Describe one way people change the environment.
Build, plant, farm, make roads or create parks
Which is an example of caring for nature?
Name one way to show texture in a drawing.
Use varied lines, marks or shading
Plan a small artwork showing nature and a built feature.
Includes both with an appropriate medium
A model keeps falling over. What could you adjust?
Its base or joins, with teacher guidance
Why should materials suit an artwork idea?
They help communicate the intended form or message

indicators.statement: Use visual art tools, materials and methods to create artworks from ideas.
questions: Which tool can make an outline?
Teacher-approved clay or safe modelling material
Which method uses repeated shapes or lines?
What is a sketch used for?
You want to make a collage. What materials are useful?
Match: drawing; weaving; modelling to making lines; interlacing materials; shaping a form.
What should you do before using an unfamiliar tool?
Ask the teacher and follow instructions
Make a small outline for an artwork you plan to create.
Name one way to use less material.
Plan first and use only what is needed
Explain why you chose a particular material.
Connects material to the artwork's purpose
A colour is unavailable. What can you do?
Choose an available colour or adapt the design
Keep tools pointed away and follow directions
Match: clean card; pencil; crayon to model base; outline; colour.
A sharp tool is required for a project. What should a learner do?
Use only with teacher supervision or select a safe alternative
Demonstrate safe use of one familiar art tool.
To keep the workspace safe and organised
Name one way to improve a first draft.
Add detail, change size or refine shape
Describe the steps you would use to make a simple artwork.
Logical sequence from plan to making
What can you do if your plan is not working?
Adapt it, ask for help or try another safe method

indicators.statement: Create visual artworks expressing ideas about local history, culture, environment or community issues.
questions: Which can be shown in a community artwork?
Name one issue an artwork could address.
Litter, flooding, road safety or teacher-provided issue
Which is a constructive poster message?
Name one feature that can make a poster clear.
Large image, readable words or strong contrast
Your drawing shows a blocked drain. What helpful action can it suggest?
Dispose of waste properly or keep drains clear
Sketch an artwork encouraging a safe community action.
Match issue to possible message: litter; unsafe crossing; polluted water.
use a bin; cross safely; protect water
Explain the message in your artwork.
Which approach is fair when showing a community problem?
Focus on the issue and solutions, not unsupported blame
How can a picture communicate without many words?
You do not know the cause of an issue. What should you do?
Use a teacher-provided fact or check a reliable source
Why include accurate details in cultural artwork?
Name one way to show local identity in art.
Verified place, object, pattern or activity
Describe an artwork idea and its intended message.
Match visual choice to effect: bold colour; simple image; readable text.
A suggested picture could shame a person. How can it be changed?
Show the issue without identifying or humiliating anyone
What should an issue-based artwork encourage?
Name one way art can help a community.
Share information or encourage helpful action
Explain a respectful community poster to a classmate.
Why is respectful wording important in public messages?

indicators.statement: Explore music, dance and drama that reflect people and community life.
questions: Name three forms of performing arts.
Describe one performance you have seen or studied in class.
Relevant detail about movement, sound or story
What can a drum help provide?
Name one safe way to make a rhythm without an instrument.
You are unfamiliar with a local performance. How can you learn about it?
Watch teacher-provided material and ask respectfully
Match: singer; dancer; actor with song; movement; character.
What can a song tell us about a community?
It may share stories, values or activities
Act a brief everyday scene using a teacher-provided prompt.
Name one way performers keep a shared rhythm.
Listen for a beat or cue
A performance portrays a culture unfamiliar to you. What should you avoid?
Mocking or copying inaccurately; ask and learn respectfully
A signal to begin or change an action
Give one example of a natural sound that could inspire music.
Rain, wind, birds or another suitable sound
Match: beginning; middle; ending to performance order.
To remember and coordinate the sequence
Show a simple movement pattern with a clear start and stop.
Narrator, rhythm keeper, organiser or designer
State one respectful way to respond to a performance.
Listen and give kind, specific feedback

indicators.statement: Plan and create music, dance or drama expressing local culture and environment.
questions: What should a group decide first when planning a performance?
The idea it wants to express
Name one sound resource for a performance.
Which movement could show flowing water?
What can a prop help communicate?
A group depicts a local story. What helps keep it accurate?
Match: voice; movement; prop with singing; dance; visual support.
Describe a safe movement showing a tree in wind.
Create a short rhythm or movement sequence about a place.
Sequence connects clearly to a place
Name one way to make performance safe.
Clear space, moderate volume and teacher guidance
Which can help a group stay together?
A shared beat or start signal
A learner prefers not to act in front of others. What role could they take?
Narrator, planner, sound maker or small-group role
Name one simple structure for a drama.
They help express the performance idea
Match: drum; shaker; voice to beat; rattling rhythm; words or singing.
A prop is heavy or unsafe. What should the group do?
Replace it with a safe lightweight prop
Explain how movement or sound expresses your idea.
What should performers do if someone is accidentally bumped?
Stop and check safety, then follow teacher guidance
Plan a short performance with one sound and one movement.
Both elements relate to a clear idea
Why should cultural performance be respectful?
It represents real people and traditions
How can you improve a performance after practice?
Listen to feedback and adjust timing or movement

indicators.statement: Use performance to communicate a topical or environmental community issue.
questions: Which issue could a short drama show?
Name one safe community message for a song or drama.
Road safety, cleanliness or care for water
What can clapping add to a performance?
How can a dance show a helpful action?
Use movements that represent the action
A scene shows unsafe crossing. How can it be staged safely?
Mime it in a clear safe space without entering traffic
Match issue with message: litter; water pollution; road safety.
use a bin; protect water; cross carefully
State the main message of a performance you plan.
Act out a respectful conversation about keeping a playground clean.
Everyone can help care for our shared space
Name one suitable prop for a safety performance.
A joke in a performance might insult a group. What should the group do?
Change it to a respectful, issue-focused message
Why use a clear repeated refrain in a song?
It helps the audience remember the message
What should performers do before using instruments?
Make a short spoken or movement message about a safe action.
Message is clear and action is safe
Match: narrator; rhythm keeper; actor with words; beat; character action.
The audience cannot understand the message. What might improve it?
Use simpler words or clearer movement
What should an issue performance aim to do?
Why should an issue be represented accurately?
So the message does not mislead
Give one kind audience response after a performance.
Specific positive comment or respectful question
How can a learner contribute without acting?
Help plan, narrate, make rhythm or prepare a safe prop

indicators.statement: Present and share a performance with an audience respectfully and safely.
questions: What helps an audience hear a performer?
A clear voice at a suitable volume
Name one way to prepare for a performance.
Practise, arrange space or check materials
What is a respectful audience response?
To keep movement clear and safe
A performer forgets what comes next. What can the group do?
Pause and prompt kindly or continue with the next part
Match: performer; audience; narrator with: acts; watches/listens; tells events.
Introduce a performance using one sentence.
Which helps a group begin together?
The performance space is cluttered. What should happen?
Pause and ask the teacher to clear or rearrange it
Name one way a performance can share learning.
It can tell a story or communicate a message
Practise thanking an audience after a performance.
What should happen to props after sharing?
It is specific, kind and suggests an improvement
Present a short piece to a partner or small group.
Shares an idea safely at an agreed level
A learner is uncomfortable performing publicly. What is appropriate?
Offer an alternative role or smaller audience without pressure
Match: practise; cue; clear space with readiness; timing; safety.
Name one thing your group did well and one improvement.
Why should performers listen to one another?
Name one support role for a presentation.
Narrator, organiser, prop helper or rhythm keeper
Why should an audience respect different performance styles?
People express ideas in different ways

indicators.statement: Plan a simple display of visual artworks for a chosen theme or audience.
questions: What should be decided when planning an exhibition?
Name one suitable place for a class display.
Classroom wall, board or teacher-approved space
It helps viewers understand their connection
Name one way to display a paper artwork.
Place on a board or hang with permission
There is little wall space. What can you do?
Select fewer works or arrange them neatly on a board
Match: theme; venue; audience with: shared idea; place; viewers.
Explain one reason to label an artwork.
The label can identify its title, maker or idea
What should be considered before inviting viewers?
Name one item that could be on an artwork label.
A displayed work may fall. What should be done?
Secure it safely with teacher help
Which display is easiest to understand?
Works arranged with space and clear labels
Why should displays include different learners' work fairly?
To recognise contributions and provide inclusion
Match: label; spacing; grouping with information; visibility; organisation.
Arrange or describe a small display of three teacher-provided artworks.
A learner's work is not selected. What is a kind response?
Acknowledge their effort and explain selection fairly
What should be avoided when mounting artwork?
Damaging it or blocking an exit
Name one way to make a display accessible.
Place it at a reachable height or provide a spoken description
Describe how your display theme connects the works.
Why prepare a display before viewers arrive?
To check order, safety and labels
What can viewers learn from a display?

indicators.statement: Plan a presentation of music, dance or drama for an audience.
questions: The idea and order of the piece
Name one thing to check in a performance space.
Clear floor, safe distance or suitable volume
Why arrange performers in a clear formation?
So actions can be seen and space is safe
A planned movement uses more space than available. What should the group do?
Adapt the movement to fit safely
Match: introduction; main part; ending with: welcome; performance content; closing.
Name one role needed to organise a performance.
Performer, narrator, rhythm keeper or organiser
Which is a safe sound level?
Name one way to include an audience respectfully.
Introduce the theme or invite quiet listening
An instrument is unavailable. What can replace its role?
Voice, clapping or another approved resource
To make changes smooth and safe
What should be done with props after rehearsal?
Match: role; cue; rehearsal with: responsibility; signal; practice.
Beginning, main action and ending are clear
A participant cannot attend the presentation. What can the group do?
Adjust roles without blame and include available contributions
Explain one way the audience will understand the performance theme.
Introduction, words, movement or clear sequence
What is a respectful audience invitation?
Please join us to watch our class performance
Why should performance participation be flexible?
Learners have different comfort levels and abilities
Which should happen before public sharing?
Name one way to improve a plan after rehearsal.

indicators.statement: Appreciate, describe and appraise own and others' visual artworks using simple criteria.
questions: The picture uses repeated curved lines
Name two features you can discuss in an artwork.
Theme, subject, material, technique, colour, shape or texture
Describe one part of an artwork you find interesting.
What is a useful way to give feedback?
Say what works and suggest one possible improvement kindly
What is the subject of an artwork?
What it shows or is about
You dislike an artwork. How can you respond respectfully?
Describe an observable feature without insulting the maker
Match: material; technique; theme with: what it is made of; how made; main idea.
Name one question to ask when appraising a work.
Why use criteria when discussing art?
To make comments thoughtful and fair
A work is useful but simple. Can it still be valued?
Yes; usefulness and design can both matter
Give one positive, specific comment about a work.
Kind comment tied to a feature
Match: rough texture; bright colour; balanced layout to observable features.
How can feedback help an artist?
It offers ideas for learning or revision
Point out or mark one repeated shape in a sample image.
Two viewers interpret a picture differently. What can they do?
Share reasons and listen to each other
How useful an artwork is for a purpose
Describe a work using subject, material and one feature.
Art is personal work and feedback should support learning
Name one change an artist might make after feedback.
Add detail, adjust colour, size, layout or technique

indicators.statement: Appreciate and discuss performances using simple observations and respectful feedback.
questions: Which is an observable feature of a performance?
Name one feature to discuss in a song or dance.
Theme, voice, rhythm, movement, costume or coordination
Describe one thing you noticed in a performance.
The clear rhythm helped me follow the song
Character, voice, gesture, story or use of space
A performance is different from what you expected. What should you do?
Watch respectfully and describe what you observed
Match: voice; movement; costume with music; dance; visual appearance.
What does rhythm help performers organise?
It helps performers know what was effective
Give one gentle suggestion for improving a performance.
A performer makes a mistake. What is a supportive response?
Match: theme; gesture; coordination with main idea; body action; working together.
Name one social or cultural value a performance might express.
Unity, respect, cooperation or another relevant value
Describe a performance using two criteria.
Two classmates disagree about a performance. What can they do?
Explain their views politely using examples
Why should audience members listen attentively?
To understand and appreciate the performance
Name one strength and one possible improvement in a teacher-provided performance.
What can a performance communicate besides a story?
An idea, feeling or community message
Keep effective choices and practise adjustments
